blocks.text: Demonstration document. Not for filing or payment.
Date: November 3, 2026. Completed by Morgan Lee for HANGS Construction Services LLC; sent by email to Tax Preparation. Not signed.

Client note: these answers are our own statements, not verified facts. The trial balance behind them is unapproved, and any document described as still being signed or not yet found should be treated as missing.
Answer: HANGS Construction Services LLC. No change.
Answer: XX-XXX4567 (demonstration; the 00 prefix is never issued).
Answer: 1200 Example Road, Anytown, WA 00000; 000-555-0100. Unchanged since formation.
4. State and form of organization; entity elections?
Answer: Washington limited liability company; certificate filed June 30, 2023, effective July 1, 2023; one general and one shareholder. No Form 8832 or section 761 election by the company.
Answer: July 1, 2023: initial cash contributions made and development work (site selection, permits) began. The first site purchase closed in July 2024; nothing was held at June 30, 2024.
Answer: June 30 since formation. First return July 1, 2023 to June 30, 2024 (initial); June 30, 2025 return filed. No Form 8716, Form 1128 or section 444 election ever.

Answer: We buy finished commercial sites from unrelated developers in Anytown, Washington, build small single-story flex industrial buildings with subcontractors and sell them to unrelated business owners; four stages so far. No subdividing, building for others, leasing, employees or other income.

Answer: Customers sign a purchase agreement only after completion and close within days; 104 units closed at $31,500 each, all cash, last in May 2026. No agreement was signed before July 1, 2025 or open at June 30, 2026; we never contract to build for a customer; no installment sales.
9. Land, work in progress or units on hand at either year end?
Answer: None at either date. Every site bought this year was built on and sold by May 2026; June 2026 costs are completion, punch-list and closing costs on sold units.

Answer: Accrual, books and returns. Internal unaudited statements; no applicable financial statement. No Form 3115 ever. We have never capitalized section 263A costs or kept an inventory; construction cost is cost of units sold when they close, as on the June 30, 2025 return.

Answer: Subcontractor progress payments $2,852,000 (site prices run through the same draw account, not separated); accrued Tallow Creek Framing TCF-2764 $9,400; Harbor Field Counsel HFC-26-0142, Stage 4 closing legal, $18,500 paid June 18, 2026; warranty provision $7,500; completion provision $1,100. Land, materials and labor cannot be split.
Answer: Twenty-two payments of $6,500 to Alder and Finch Realty, the unrelated listing broker, for sales commissions. Nothing else.

Answer: One-year construction warranty per unit. Opening $11,600 covered prior-year units; six $700 claims ($4,200) went to repair subcontractors for repair work on them, none settled in cash with customers. The $7,500 at June 30, 2026 is our estimate for this year's units. Post-year-end work not yet summarized.

Answer: Opening $700: punch-list work on prior-year units by a subcontractor, paid September 30, 2025. The $1,100 at June 30, 2026: estimated punch-list work on units closed May 2026, on the units themselves. No obligation for common improvements; sites were bought finished.
15. June 30, 2025 return: reserves and organization cost.

Answer: It added back all $12,300 of reserves and deducted none; no recurring item exception or alternative cost method. Its Schedule M-1 showed an organization cost reversal of $480.00 against the $480.33 deducted on the first return; the $0.33 is unexplained. Keep it open; do not plug.
Answer: $480.33 total (Washington filing fee and legal), paid July 2023, deducted in full on the June 30, 2024 return. Nothing capitalized or amortized; no election to capitalize.

Answer: June 30, 2025: $12,700, Tallow Creek Framing TCF-2291, deducted on that year's return, paid August 12, 2025. June 30, 2026: $9,400, Tallow Creek Framing TCF-2764, framing completion finished June 2026. No related-party payees.
Answer: Never borrowed; no shareholder loans; no debt canceled or modified; no interest expense or income.

Answer: Since July 1, 2023, unchanged: HANGS Property Holdings LLC, shareholder, 99.9%; HANGS Construction Services LLC, officer, 0.1%; one percentage for profit, loss and capital, as on earlier returns. The signed agreement is still being circulated; treat the percentages as draft. No guarantees, deficit restoration obligations or special allocations; cash contributions only; no interest ever sold or exchanged.

Answer: Washington LLC organized June 15, 2023; sole member Morgan Lee; Form 8832 corporate election effective that date, IRS acceptance on file. EIN XX-XXX6789 (demonstration); same address as HANGS. Domestic C corporation, June 30 year, Forms 1120 filed since the short year ended June 30, 2023; no S election. Holds only its HANGS interest; no receipts; never required to file Schedule M-3.

Answer: Washington corporation incorporated June 15, 2023; sole shareholder Morgan Lee. EIN XX-XXX5678 (demonstration); same address. Domestic C corporation, June 30 year, Forms 1120 filed for the same periods; no S election. Acts only as HANGS's officer; no receipts; never required to file Schedule M-3. President Morgan Lee is authorized by its bylaws and Washington law to sign for it.

Answer: U.S. citizen; SSN XXX-XX-1234 (demonstration; area 000 is never issued); 1200 Example Road, Anytown, WA 00000; U.S. phone 000-555-0100. No other trade or business; no other entity with gross receipts.
Answer: None: no shareholder or owner paid for services; no guaranteed payments, employees, payroll, Forms W-2 or benefit plans.
Answer: Cash on June 30, 2026: $239,760 to HANGS Property Holdings LLC, $240 to HANGS Construction Services LLC. No earlier draws, no property. Signed dividend authorization still being collected.

Answer: No contributions this year. Book capital $0 at June 30, 2025, $4,500 at June 30, 2026. Tax-basis capital on the June 30, 2025 shareholder statements: $12,287.37 (Holdings LLC), $12.30 (officer Inc).
Answer: No; the export is still marked unapproved.

Answer: None: no foreign accounts (2025), trusts, shareholders, operations, payees, Forms 1042/1042-S, specified foreign financial assets or entity interests; no digital assets received, held or sold in 2025.

Answer: HANGS owns no stock or entity interest; is not publicly traded; interests were never offered publicly or in a registered offering. No reportable transaction, section 754 election, basis adjustment, like-kind exchange, undivided-interest dividend, 1.707-8 transfer, opportunity fund, foreign acquisition, stock repurchase, 163(j) election, pass-through interest or hybrid arrangement. Purpose: building and selling commercial units only.

Answer: For 2024 payments: seven Forms 1099-NEC (six subcontractors and the broker, none incorporated), due January 31, 2025, filed January 2025. For 2025 payments: Forms 1099-NEC filed January 2026. The only other return required in calendar 2025 was the June 30, 2025 Form 1165. No Forms W-2, 941, 940 or excise returns.
Answer: Not electing out this year. tax matters representative HANGS Construction Services LLC; designated individual Morgan Lee; both at the address and phone in answer 3.
31. Signer; may the IRS discuss the return with the preparer?
Answer: Morgan Lee, President of HANGS Construction Services LLC, the officer. Yes.
Answer: Form 7004 filed September 9, 2026 through our accounting software; acknowledgment not yet located; no disallowance notice.
Answer: Yes; Stage 5 sites planned for the year ending June 30, 2027. Not winding up; not a final return.
Answer: Only HFC-26-0142 so far; support for the 920 progress payments, 22 commissions and six warranty claims is not yet assembled.
35. Where is the business carried on? State information?
Answer: All sites, construction and sales are in Washington. No state or local tax information supplied.
Answer: Both current liabilities; work expected within twelve months.

Answer: Year ended June 30, 2025: contract revenue $2,840,000; book income $70,000; ordinary business income per return $82,780. Year ended June 30, 2024: no income; one $480.33 organization cost deduction.
39. Were losses ever allocated to a shareholder?
Answer: Only the $480.33 loss for the year ended June 30, 2024, allocated 99.9% to Holdings LLC and 0.1% to officer Inc. The years ended June 30, 2025 and 2026 had income and no loss.
Answer: None other than the dividends in answer 24.

trail.result: Read FY2026 trial balance.xlsx.
Read FY2026 general ledger.xlsx: 2,125 lines.
Read FY2026 financial statements.pdf.
Read June 2026 bank reconciliation.xlsx: prepared by Morgan Lee on July 9, 2026, 5 outstanding payments and 1 unrecorded charge; no reviewer has signed it.

trail.what: Recompute cash from every ledger line and agree it to the trial balance, the statements and the reconciliation
trail.result: One cash account, 100110 at Cinderbrook Bank. Its 1,058 ledger lines ($25,000.00 opening, 104 receipts, 953 payments) add up to $29,900.00, the trial balance, the statements' cash and the balance per books on Morgan Lee's reconciliation. The export itself says “draft and unapproved”.

trail.what: Propose materiality from book income, as the cash audit plan sets it
trail.result: Book income $244,500.00 x 5% = $12,225.00, rounded down to $12,000.00, the same as the year-end audit. Performance materiality $9,000.00; clearly trivial $600.00. Cash is $29,900.00, so a single misstatement of cash could matter only through what it hides. The engagement shareholder sets the final amounts.

Balance per bank $42,300.00 less 5 outstanding payments of $13,100.00 is $29,200.00; balance per books $29,900.00 less $700.00 of bank charges not yet recorded is $29,200.00. It foots with no difference, but no reviewer has signed it.
Cash $29,900.00 agrees across the books · materiality $12,000.00 proposed · the reconciliation foots but is unreviewed
Read Bank confirmation request.pdf: sent October 28, 2026, authorized by Morgan Lee, replies to the audit team only.
Read Cinderbrook Bank confirmation.pdf: signed by Casey Morrow on October 30, 2026 and sent to the audit team directly.
Read Cinderbrook Bank supplementary reply.pdf: signed by Casey Morrow on November 2, 2026 and sent to the audit team directly.

trail.what: Check that the audit team sent the request and the bank answered the audit team directly
trail.result: The audit team sent the request on October 28, 2026, authorized by Morgan Lee on October 27, 2026, asking the bank to reply to the audit team only. Casey Morrow answered on October 30, 2026 and November 2, 2026, for the same account (Operating account ending 4471) as of June 30, 2026. Nothing passed through the client.

trail.what: Compare the balance the bank confirmed with the client's books
trail.result: The request showed the books' $29,900.00; the bank did not change it to agree and confirmed $42,300.00. The $12,400.00 difference must be explained by items the bank and the books recorded on different days, or it is an error. The bank reports no loans, lines of credit, guarantees or other accounts.

trail.what: Read the bank's answers to the further questions
trail.result: Service charges in the year: $700.00, one annual treasury services fee for 2026, debited January 2, 2026; no others. Check 1043 ($700.00): not presented; no stop payment on file. Checks are stale after 180 days. Holds, liens, set-off and compensating balances: none.
The bank confirmed $42,300.00 directly · $12,400.00 more than the books, to explain · no loans or other accounts
Read June 2026 bank statement.pdf: 64 items, closing at $42,300.00.

trail.what: Agree the confirmed balance to the June statement and to the reconciliation
trail.result: The confirmed $42,300.00 is the June statement's closing balance and the reconciliation's balance per bank; the reconciliation's balance per books is the trial balance's $29,900.00.

trail.what: Match every June payment in the ledger to the June statement, then recompute the reconciliation
trail.result: Of the ledger's 64 June payments, 60 are on the June statement and 4 sent June 29 and June 30, $12,400.00, are not. Those 4 are the reconciliation's June items. Its other outstanding payment is older: check 1043, HC-WCL-03 (warranty claim paid), $700.00, recorded December 3, 2025. Adjusted bank $29,200.00 equals adjusted books $29,200.00 only after the $700.00 bank charge the books never recorded.
The confirmation agrees with the June statement and the reconciliation · 4 June payments outstanding · one older check · one unrecorded charge
Read July 2026 bank statement.pdf: 7 items, closing at $15,250.00.

trail.what: Trace every outstanding payment to the July statement
trail.result: All 4 June payments cleared July 1 and July 2, $12,400.00, at the amounts sent. Check 1043 ($700.00) is on neither statement and the bank says it was not presented; no stop payment on file: it was 209 days old at June 30, past the bank's 180 days, so it is stale. The warranty claim is in the books as paid, but the unit owner has not been paid.

trail.what: Search every cash line in the books for the bank's charge
trail.result: The bank debited $700.00 on January 2, 2026 (annual treasury services fee for 2026). None of the 1,058 cash lines in the books is a bank charge, so it was never recorded: cash and book income are both overstated by $700.00. The reconciliation carried it as a reconciling item instead of booking it.

trail.what: Explain the confirmation difference item by item
trail.result: The $12,400.00 the bank confirmed above the books is the 4 payments that cleared in July ($12,400.00), plus check 1043 that was never presented ($700.00), less the bank charge the books never recorded ($700.00). Nothing is left unexplained. The last two are the same size and cancel, which is why cash appeared to tie with only the July clearings in view.
4 payments cleared in July · check 1043 is stale · the $700.00 bank charge was never recorded · the difference is explained
Read Marshgate Project Closeout Report.xlsx: 104 closings, sent by the escrow company directly to the audit team.

trail.what: Test the wires, transfers and receipts either side of June 30
trail.result: $239,760.00 to HANGS Property Holdings LLC and $240.00 to HANGS Construction Services LLC left by wire on June 30, 2026 and are in the books that day; together $240,000.00, the dividends in the trial balance. There are no transfers to test: one account at the bank, one cash account in the books. The 3 other July payments are not in the June books. The last receipt was the closing of May 7, 2026, wired $31,500.00 as the escrow report shows; no receipts in June on either side.

trail.what: Look for cash that is held back, pledged or restricted, and what the statements would need to say
trail.result: The bank reports no holds, liens, pledges, set-off or compensating balance, and no loans whose terms could restrict cash. The escrow company wired all 104 closings in full, $3,276,000.00, so nothing is held back for the seller. The statements show one cash line, $29,900.00, all of total assets. No restricted cash, so the statements need no restricted cash disclosure; the CPA decides.
Wires and receipts are in the right year · no transfers · no restricted cash

trail.what: Add up what was found and set it against materiality
trail.result: Known misstatements add up to $700.00, 5.8% of the $12,000.00 materiality and under performance materiality of $9,000.00: the unrecorded bank charge (FEE-01). Proposed: debit a bank charges expense, credit cash. If the client declines, it goes on the summary of passed adjustments. Voiding stale check 1043 would put $700.00 back in cash against the warranty liability (STALE-01), so the two together leave cash at $29,900.00. Concluding is the CPA's job; the machine stops here.

checks.title: FEE-01
checks.detail: The bank's $700.00 annual treasury services fee for 2026 of January 2, 2026 was never recorded. Cash and book income are overstated by $700.00. Proposed adjustment: debit a bank charges expense (the trial balance has no such account yet), credit 100110 Cash. It is 5.8% of materiality and under performance materiality, so if the client declines to record it the CPA may pass it and list it on the summary of passed adjustments. The machine never posts.

checks.title: STALE-01
checks.detail: Check 1043, $700.00, for warranty claim HC-WCL-03 of December 3, 2025, has never been presented and was 209 days old at June 30, past the bank's 180-day limit. The unit owner has not been paid, yet the books count the claim as paid. Ask Morgan Lee to contact the unit owner and reissue it or void it with a stop payment. If voided: debit 100110 Cash, credit 220510 Warranty liability (or an unclaimed property liability). Cash rises by the same amount the bank charge lowers it.

checks.title: CONF-01
checks.detail: The bank confirmed $42,300.00; the request showed the books' $29,900.00. The $12,400.00 difference is explained in full: 4 June payments that cleared July 1 and July 2 ($12,400.00), plus check 1043 ($700.00), less the unrecorded bank charge ($700.00). No adjustment beyond FEE-01 and STALE-01. The CPA accepts the explanation or asks for more.

checks.title: REC-01
checks.detail: The June 30 reconciliation was prepared by Morgan Lee on July 9, 2026 and no one has signed it as reviewed. It carried a bank charge for six months instead of recording it, and a stale check without follow-up. Ask who reviews the reconciliation each month; the CPA weighs it as a control observation.
